# Canton Hyland

> Canton Hyland Hardware & Building Material Co., Ltd. manufactures architectural door hardware in Guangdong, China — panic
> exit devices, mortise lock cases, lever handles, door closers, hinges and bathroom
> accessories — and exports to distributors and project buyers in Europe, North America,
> South America, Turkey and Southeast Asia.

This site is a product and company reference. Orders are not placed here: inquiries
go to the export team by email, or through the company's Alibaba storefront.

## Key facts

- Manufacturer, not a trading company. Operating since 1998.
- 549 published models across 17 categories.
- Our stamping plant is certified to ISO 9001:2015 (certificate 69125Q0026****, valid to 29 October 2028).
- Test reports are published per model, not per range — see the download center.

## Product categories

- [Panic Exit Devices](https://cantonlock.com/products/panic-exit-devices/): Push bars and touch bars for escape routes, including fire-door, alarmed, double-door and two-point locking versions. 44 models.
- [Night Latches & Rim Locks](https://cantonlock.com/products/night-latches-rim-locks/): Surface-mounted night latches and rim locks, most with a 60mm backset, fitted through a single cylinder hole in an existing door. 25 models.
- [Stainless Steel Handles](https://cantonlock.com/products/stainless-steel-handles/): Stainless steel lever handles, including the 9000 series for doors of 35–50mm, and a concealed sliding-door handle. 43 models.
- [Lever Handles](https://cantonlock.com/products/lever-handles/): Tubular lever handle sets, mostly zinc alloy, for entrance, privacy and passage doors, with a 60/70mm backset and keying alike with deadbolts. 49 models.
- [Knob Locks](https://cantonlock.com/products/knob-locks/): Cylindrical and tubular knob locks for entry, privacy, passage and communication functions. 59 models.
- [Bathroom Accessories](https://cantonlock.com/products/bathroom-accessories/): Bathroom accessories, most of them published in stainless steel. 42 models.
- [Care Grab Bars](https://cantonlock.com/products/care-grab-bars/): Grab bars and a fold-down shower seat for accessible bathrooms: straight, knurled and angled bars fixed to the wall, and bars that flip up out of the way. 8 models.
- [Brass & Steel Door Hinges](https://cantonlock.com/products/brass-steel-hinges/): Brass, stainless-steel and steel hinge ranges for architectural door applications. 30 models.
- [Deadbolts](https://cantonlock.com/products/deadbolts/): Single- and double-cylinder deadbolts with a 25mm throw, an anti-saw roller insert and a 60/70mm adjustable backset. 12 models.
- [Door Closers](https://cantonlock.com/products/door-closers/): Door closers with aluminum bodies for commercial doors, plus a floor hinge for timber doors. 7 models.
- [Grip Handle Sets](https://cantonlock.com/products/grip-handle-sets/): Grip, pull and concealed handle sets for entrance and sliding doors. 14 models.
- [Glass Door Accessories](https://cantonlock.com/products/glass-door-accessories/): Patch fittings and pull handles for frameless glass-door assemblies. 23 models.
- [Hardware Accessories](https://cantonlock.com/products/hardware-accessories/): Door viewers, stoppers, transfer devices, bolts, indicators, latches and guards. 69 models.
- [Lock Cases](https://cantonlock.com/products/lock-cases/): Mortise lock cases in multiple backset, centre-distance and bolt configurations. 48 models.
- [Lock Cylinders](https://cantonlock.com/products/lock-cylinders/): Profile and keyed cylinders, including master-key system applications. 45 models.
- [Sliding Hook Locks](https://cantonlock.com/products/sliding-hook-locks/): Hook-lock hardware for sliding doors and narrow-stile applications. 3 models.
- [Floor Springs and Door Pivots](https://cantonlock.com/products/floor-springs-and-pivots/): Concealed floor springs, adjustable top pivots and glass top patch fittings for pivot-hung timber, metal and frameless glass doors. 28 models.

## Guides and articles

### Buying guides — dimension charts, code cross-references and selection

- [Exit Device Locking Method 2026: Rim, Surface Vertical Rod, Concealed Vertical Rod or Mortise, and Where Each One Fits](https://cantonlock.com/guides/exit-device-locking-method-2026/): An exit device is chosen twice: once for the people who will use it, and once for how it latches the door. Rim devices latch at one point into the frame and suit single doors and pairs with a mullion. Surface and concealed vertical rods latch at the head and the floor and suit pairs without a mullion, at the cost of a floor strike to keep clear. Mortise devices latch through a lock case in the door edge. This guide sets out where each fits, what EN 1125 and UL 305 say about the configuration, and which of our devices is which. Models: 300, 302, 316-D, 308-D, 320, 307, 072, 311.
- [Fire Door Annual Inspection 2026: The Hardware Items That Fail, from Closers and Latches to Labels, Under NFPA 80 and the EN Standards](https://cantonlock.com/guides/fire-door-annual-inspection-hardware-2026/): Many annual fire door inspection findings are hardware rather than the door itself: a closer that no longer latches the leaf, a latch that misses its strike, a door wedged open, a label painted over, a replacement part that was never rated, a pair that closes in the wrong order. This guide takes each finding in turn, under NFPA 80 in the United States and the EN standards and national rules in Europe, and says what normally puts it right. Models: DC01, DC02, DSL02.
- [Importing Door Hardware from China into Mexico 2026: Padrón de Importadores, Customs Broker, Pedimento, Tariff Classification and NOM Labeling](https://cantonlock.com/guides/importing-door-hardware-china-mexico-2026/): Importing locks, hinges and other door hardware from China into Mexico follows a fixed public procedure: an active RFC and registration in the SAT's Padrón de Importadores, a customs broker authorized through an encargo conferido, a pedimento under the correct fracción arancelaria, the tariff in force in 2026 for countries without a trade agreement with Mexico, NOM-050 commercial labeling where it applies, origin documents and an Incoterm that matches who imports. This guide walks through each step without quoting rates, because the rate that counts is the one in force for your fracción when you import.
- [Copper Hinges or Brass Hinges? What a Copper Hinge Is When You Order Door Hinges](https://cantonlock.com/guides/copper-or-brass-hinges-2026/): A "copper hinge" that carries a door is brass, copper alloyed with zinc; antique copper is a finish, not a metal. Two of our hinges publish brass as their material: the B024, offered from 2.0 to 3.5mm thick, and the B025. This page explains what the phrase can mean and what to write on the order so the hinge that arrives is the one you meant. Models: B024, B025.
- [Cylindrical and Tubular Lock Comparison 2026: Four Families, Every Series, and What Heavy Duty Actually Changes](https://cantonlock.com/guides/cylindrical-and-tubular-lock-comparison-2026/): 59 knob and lever locks for bored doors, in four families: tubular, light-duty cylindrical, heavy-duty cylindrical and commercial. Side by side from their specification rows, with the one row that does not separate them, and the rows that do. Models: 575 SSET, 592 PBET, 607 SSET, 578 SSET, 587 SSBK, 5831 SSET, 5870 ACET, 5874 ACET (+2).
- [Exit Device Comparison 2026: Every Push Bar in the Range by Length, Latching and Door](https://cantonlock.com/guides/exit-device-comparison-2026/): 44 records sit in our panic exit device family, and only 26 of them are exit devices. Apart from the 315 pry latch and the ABS-and-aluminum 311, every one has an aluminum alloy body and an iron push bar, so the three tables (single doors, pairs, special purposes) compare what differs: length, latching and door, with the missing rows named. Models: 300, 302, 307, 309-D, 311, 314, 315, 316-D (+2).
- [Mortise Lock Case Comparison 2026: Every Published Backset and Center Distance, Side by Side](https://cantonlock.com/guides/mortise-lock-case-comparison-2026/): 34 of our mortise lock cases publish both a backset and a center distance. Here they are in two tables, narrow-stile and standard, with the naming traps and the gaps stated plainly. Models: LC07 85×45mm, LC14 85×50mm, LC04 85*60, LC8530PS, LC33-5572, LC9230.
- [Backset and Door Thickness Chart 2026: What 589 Published Models Actually Take](https://cantonlock.com/guides/backset-door-thickness-chart-2026/): Two numbers decide whether a replacement lock drops into a door that is already machined: the backset and the door thickness range. This is what our published catalog actually carries (counted from the records rather than quoted from a brochure) with the imperial equivalents, the measuring method, and the one dimension that is not a backset and gets confused with it. Models: LC02 85×40mm, LC04 85*60, LC14 85×50mm.
- [Brass Hardware 2026: Which Brass, Why Lead Is In It, and the One Failure Mode That Decides Coastal Projects](https://cantonlock.com/guides/brass-alloys-and-dezincification-2026/): Above roughly 37% zinc, brass becomes more vulnerable to dezincification, so a cylinder on an external door, above all near the coast, should be DZR brass (CZ132 or CW602N); a dry interior door does not need it. This page sets out the brasses used in door hardware, explains why lead is in most of them and what the low-lead alternatives cost, describes dezincification and where DZR brass is genuinely required, separates brass from bronze, and counts what our own catalog publishes.
- [Validating a Hardware Certificate 2026: The Seven Parts, DoP and CE Marking, and the Six Red Flags](https://cantonlock.com/guides/certification-and-test-validation-2026/): A genuine test certificate carries 7 parts: the issuing laboratory with its address, its accreditation reference, the standard with its year, a report or certificate number, the date of issue and validity, the scope of application, and the tested configuration. The scope is the part most often missing, and checking all 7 takes about 5 minutes. This page also explains accreditation versus certification and CE marking with a Declaration of Performance, lists 6 red flags, and states what we hold: our 307 and 311 exit devices do not hold certificates today, and until certificate numbers exist we claim no rating for them. Models: 307, 311.
- [Chrome, Satin Chrome and Satin Nickel 2026: Why Two Suppliers' "Polished Chrome" Do Not Match, and How to Specify One That Does](https://cantonlock.com/guides/chrome-finish-differences-2026/): Chrome is a thin top layer over nickel, which is why nickel decides how it looks and how long it lasts. This page explains the plating stack, separates polished chrome from satin chrome from satin nickel by the property that actually distinguishes them, gives the codes, and shows from our own 336 finish rows why a finish written as a name rather than a code cannot be reordered. Models: 70722 DC, 65SN.
- [Lock Function Selection 2026: A Decision Table by Room Type, and the Two Questions That Settle Every Opening](https://cantonlock.com/guides/commercial-lock-function-decision-2026/): Pick a lock function from 2 questions: who may come in from outside, and how the person inside gets out, which must be without a key and in one motion. Corridors take passage, main entrances take entrance (keyed outside), WCs take privacy, storerooms take storeroom, classrooms take classroom and escape stairs take an exit device. This page gives the full decision table by room, the 3 function errors that become life-safety problems, such as a double-cylinder deadbolt on an escape route, and how many models of each function our catalog carries.
- [Container Loading for Door Hardware 2026: Why a 40HQ Does Not Hold More Than a 40GP](https://cantonlock.com/guides/container-loading-door-hardware-2026/): Door hardware is a weight-limited cargo, not a volume-limited one. Worked from our own shipping worksheet: the median carton density is 614 kg per cubic meter, which is above the point where a 40-foot container runs out of payload before it runs out of space. The high cube buys about 13 per cent more volume and, for this cargo, no more hardware. Models: 607 SSET.
- [Corrosion Resistance 2026: EN 1670 Grades 0–5, Salt Spray Hours, and What the Test Does Not Tell You](https://cantonlock.com/guides/corrosion-resistance-en-1670-2026/): EN 1670 grades door hardware corrosion resistance from 0 to 5, and each grade is a number of hours in a neutral salt spray cabinet. This page gives the hours for every grade, explains what ASTM B117 and ANSI/BHMA A156.18 do on the other side of the Atlantic, names the three environments where a grade chosen by habit fails, and is honest about what a cabinet test cannot predict.
- [200,000 Cycles: What a Durability Figure Means in EN 1906 and in ANSI/BHMA, and Why It Is Not the Same Number](https://cantonlock.com/guides/cycle-testing-durability-grades-2026/): We publish 200,000 cycles on 132 models. In EN 1906 that is the top durability category. In ANSI/BHMA A156.2 it is the entry grade. Both statements are true, and a specification that reads one as the other will either over-buy or under-buy. This page sets out what a cycle test actually is, what each scale asks for, and where our own figure sits on both. Models: LC02 85×40mm, LH851, 607 SSET.
- [Dimensional Interchangeability 2026: The Seven Dimensions That Decide Whether a Lock Drops In, and How Many We Publish](https://cantonlock.com/guides/dimensional-interchangeability-2026/): "Is it interchangeable?" is answered by seven dimensions, and two of them are the ones almost nobody publishes. This page lists them in the order they cause failures, explains why matching the backset is not enough, sets out what to send a factory when you want a drop-in for a discontinued lock, and counts how many of our own 255 lock products publish each dimension, including the one at three per cent.
- [Door Closer Mounting 2026: Regular Arm, Top Jamb, Parallel Arm and Slide Track Compared](https://cantonlock.com/guides/door-closer-mounting-positions-2026/): A door closer mounts in 4 standard ways: regular arm (pull side, the most efficient, with the arm in the opening), top jamb (on the frame, push side, for glazed or narrow-stile doors), parallel arm (push side, arm tucked against the door, the institutional choice) and slide track (the flattest). Parallel arm gives the closer less leverage, so a closer sized for a regular arm can stop latching the door when mounted parallel: if parallel arm is likely, say so when the power size is chosen. This page also covers reinforcement, handing and backcheck. Models: JU-088.
- [Door Closer Power Size 2026: EN 1154 Sizes 1–7, A156.4, and How to Pick One from the Door](https://cantonlock.com/guides/door-closer-power-size-2026/): A door closer is specified by a power size, and the power size is derived from the door (its leaf width and its mass) not from the opening or the building type. This page sets out the EN 1154 size ladder with the leaf widths each covers, how the ANSI/BHMA A156.4 approach differs, the three adjustments that are not the power size, and the accessibility constraint that overrides all of it. Models: JU-088, JU-051, JU-072, JU-093.
- [Door Hardware HS Codes 2026: Headings 8301 and 8302 Decoded, and Where the Six Digits Stop](https://cantonlock.com/guides/door-hardware-hs-codes-2026/): Almost every product in a door hardware catalog classifies under one of two HS headings: 8301 for locks and keys, 8302 for mountings and fittings. This page sets out the subheadings under each, names the four that are most often got wrong (door closers, keys shipped separately, parts, and furniture versus building fittings) and explains exactly where the internationally agreed code ends and your own country's begins.
- [Door Preparation 2026: The 161 Bore, the 86 Mortise Pocket, and What "Prepped For" Actually Guarantees](https://cantonlock.com/guides/door-preparation-161-and-86-2026/): A door arrives on site "prepped", and whether the lock fits is decided by holes cut weeks earlier in another factory. This page sets out the standard bored-lock and mortise-lock preparations with their dimensions, explains the ANSI/BHMA A115 series that governs them, and lists the five things a purchase order has to say before a door manufacturer can cut anything.
- [Door Thickness to Cylinder Length 2026: The Arithmetic, a Lookup Table, and Why the Answer Is Often Rounded Up](https://cantonlock.com/guides/door-thickness-to-cylinder-length-2026/): Each half of a euro cylinder is half the door thickness plus the escutcheon depth on that side, rounded up to the 5mm ladder that starts at 27.5mm: a 40mm door with 4mm escutcheons comes to 55mm and is ordered as 56mm. This page gives the calculation, a door-thickness lookup table worked against the nine lengths we actually publish, explains why a thin door still gets a protruding cylinder, and shows what changes when the lock case is not centered in the leaf.
- [EN 1125 or EN 179 in 2026: Panic Bar or Emergency Lever, and the One Question About People That Decides It](https://cantonlock.com/guides/en-1125-vs-en-179-2026/): Two European standards cover escape hardware and they are chosen by who uses the building, not by how important the door is. This page explains what separates EN 1125 from EN 179, gives the occupancy test that decides between them, decodes the classification digits, lists the three mistakes that produce a non-compliant opening, and states what our own exit range does and does not hold. Models: 307, 311.
- [EN to ANSI/BHMA Cross-Reference 2026: What Maps, What Does Not, and Why](https://cantonlock.com/guides/en-ansi-bhma-cross-reference-2026/): Specifiers ask for a conversion table between EN and ANSI/BHMA door hardware standards. What exists is a scope map, not an equivalence: the two systems classify different properties, and a product certified to one carries no automatic claim under the other. This page sets out which standard covers which product family on each side, what each one measures, and the four places the mapping genuinely breaks. Models: 300, 305, 307, 311.
- [Euro Cylinder Size Chart 2026: Every Length and Split, and How to Measure Yours](https://cantonlock.com/guides/euro-cylinder-size-chart-2026/): A euro cylinder is described by two numbers, and getting them the wrong way round is the commonest ordering error in door hardware. This is the full size chart to EN 1303 and DIN 18252 geometry, the nine overall lengths we publish, the split combinations that add up to each one, and the measurement that decides which you need. Models: 45BN, 65SN, 70BK, 70MB.
- [Exit Device Outside Trim 2026: Every Trim Function Compared, Dogging Rules, and Why the Bar Is Never the Decision](https://cantonlock.com/guides/exit-device-outside-trim-functions-2026/): The bar inside always lets people out; the outside trim decides who gets in, whether the door can be held unlocked in business hours, and whether it still complies in a fire. Dogging, which holds the latch retracted, is forbidden on any fire exit device, because a fire door works by staying latched. This page compares every outside trim function, the 4 device types and the trims each takes, mechanical versus cylinder dogging, and how many of our 15 outside trims publish their function. Models: 307, 311.
- [Finish Code Reference 2026: The 23 Codes, the BHMA Numbers, and the Four Pairs That Reverse](https://cantonlock.com/guides/finish-code-reference-2026/): A finish code on a purchase order decides what arrives, and four pairs of codes in common use are reversals of each other. This is the reference: the 23 codes our catalog uses, how they line up with BHMA 600-series and US26x numbers, the pairs that get transposed, and a count of how inconsistently our own catalog spells them. Models: LH851, LH852 BNBK, 70SN.
- [Fire Door Hardware 2026: Which Components Must Be Rated, EN 1634-1 vs UL 10C and NFPA 252, and What a Certificate Covers](https://cantonlock.com/guides/fire-door-hardware-what-must-be-rated-2026/): Everything fixed to or cut into a fire door has to be part of the tested assembly: the hinges, the lock or latch, the closer, intumescent and smoke seals, exit devices, glazing and beads, flush bolts and coordinators on pairs, and the fixings. A certificate covers only the configuration and scope that were tested, and an EN 1634-1 classification is not a UL 10C listing. Our 307 and 311 exit devices do not hold certificates today; until certificate numbers exist we do not claim a fire rating for them. Models: 307, 311.
- [Glass Door Hardware 2026: Thickness Ranges, Cut-Out Dimensions, and the One Step That Cannot Be Undone](https://cantonlock.com/guides/glass-door-thickness-and-cutouts-2026/): Our glass fittings take glass from 8mm to 14mm, each model within its own stated range, and every hole and cut-out must be made before the glass is toughened, because after toughening it cannot be drilled. This page gives the glass thickness ranges our fittings actually accept, explains the glass gap dimension and the corner radius on a cut-out, sets out why every hole must be made before toughening, and lists what has to be on the glass shop drawing before anybody orders anything.
- [Door Hardware Refurbishment Survey 2026: The Fourteen Fields, What Needs a Screwdriver, and How to Sample a Building You Cannot Fully Open](https://cantonlock.com/guides/hardware-refurbishment-survey-2026/): Survey the doors, not the drawings, and record 14 fields per leaf. Fields 1 to 7 and 12 to 14 come from the corridor with a caliper and a phone; fields 8, 9 and 11 need the lock or cylinder out, which is why sampling exists. This page lists the 14 fields and why each one decides an order, gives a sampling rule by door type, and shows how the survey becomes an order.
- [Door Hardware Warranty 2026: What "Ten Year" Actually Covers, the Five Exclusions That Do the Work, and How to Make a Claim Succeed](https://cantonlock.com/guides/hardware-warranty-what-it-covers-2026/): A warranty is decided by its exclusions, not its number of years, and 5 exclusions defeat most claims: improper installation (the largest by far), an unsuitable environment such as a 201 stainless lever on a coastal door, the wrong cleaner on a plated finish, modification, and ordinary wear. This page separates warranty from guarantee and statutory rights, sets out what a successful claim contains, and says what a factory can honestly promise about a part it will never see again.
- [Hinge Grades and Hinge Count 2026: EN 1935 Grades 1–14, ANSI/BHMA A156.1, and How Many a Door Needs](https://cantonlock.com/guides/hinge-grades-and-count-2026/): Two questions decide a hinge specification: what grade, and how many. EN 1935 answers the first with grades 1 to 14 tied to a tested door mass; ANSI/BHMA A156.1 answers it with a weight class and a frequency. Neither answers the second, which is governed by leaf height and mass. This page sets out both ladders, the count rule, and the three failure modes that come from getting the count right and the grade wrong.
- [Key Blanks and Restricted Profiles 2026: Open, Restricted and Patented Keyways, and What Key Control Actually Buys](https://cantonlock.com/guides/key-blanks-and-restricted-profiles-2026/): A keyway is open, restricted or patented. Open blanks are sold everywhere and a copy takes 2 minutes; restricted blanks reach only authorized dealers, a contractual control; patented blanks are a legal monopoly that ends when the patent expires, so a system specified years ago may no longer be protected. None of the three makes a cylinder harder to pick or drill. This page also lists what to decide before a master key system is cut. Models: 65SN, 70BK.
- [Lever Return and EN 1906 2026: Why a Lever Must Curve Back, and What the Eight-Digit Classification Says](https://cantonlock.com/guides/lever-return-and-en-1906-2026/): A straight lever handle looks cleaner than a returned one and is rejected on most commercial specifications, for a reason that has nothing to do with taste. This page explains what lever return is, the safety and accessibility requirements behind it, why a knob fails accessibility where a lever passes, and how to read the eight fields of an EN 1906 handle classification instead of quoting only the first one.
- [Master Key Hierarchy Planning 2026: The Levels, What Cross-Keying Really Costs, and How to Leave Room for the Building You Will Have](https://cantonlock.com/guides/master-key-hierarchy-planning-2026/): A master key system has up to 5 levels (GGMK, GMK, MK, SMK and the change key), and most buildings need 3 at most. Every extra level and every cross-keyed door spends combinations from a finite pool, which is why systems run out. This page sets out the hierarchy, the 5 questions to answer before a cylinder is cut, vertical versus horizontal designs, and how to reserve room for the building to grow. Models: 578 SSET, 3431 SSET.
- [Material Traceability 2026: EN 10204 Types 2.1, 2.2, 3.1 and 3.2, Heat Numbers, and What a Hardware Factory Can Honestly Trace](https://cantonlock.com/guides/material-traceability-mill-certs-2026/): "Send the material certificate" means four different documents, and the difference between them is who signed it and whether the test was on your metal. This page sets out the EN 10204 document types, explains heat numbers and where the chain of custody genuinely breaks in small hardware, separates material traceability from RoHS and REACH compliance, and says which of these a door hardware factory can honestly provide.
- [Powder Coating and RAL 2026: Why a Color Number Does Not Specify a Finish, What Pretreatment Decides, and What to Write on the Order](https://cantonlock.com/guides/powder-coating-and-ral-2026/): A RAL number sets the hue only: gloss is specified separately (ISO 2813), architectural powder film typically runs 60–80 µm, and threads must be masked because a coated M5 thread may not take an M5 screw. This page explains what RAL specifies and what it leaves open, why pretreatment decides whether a coating survives, where powder coating fails on hardware geometry, which tests are worth citing, and the four lines that make a finish orderable.
- [Qualifying a Hardware Supplier 2026: Factory, Trader or Broker, the Five Questions That Separate Them, and What to Verify](https://cantonlock.com/guides/qualifying-a-hardware-supplier-2026/): 5 questions separate a factory from a trading company or a broker: which models do you make yourselves; can you change the backset on this model, and what would the tooling cost; who does your plating; what is the minimum in one finish, and why; and can we have the dimensioned drawing. A factory answers each at once or with a reason. This page also lists what can be verified independently and what a first order should be. Models: 307, 311.
- [Samples and Incoming Inspection 2026: The Golden Sample, What to Measure, and What a Sample Cannot Tell You](https://cantonlock.com/guides/samples-and-incoming-inspection-2026/): Ask for a pre-production sample whenever anything differs from the catalog, and make it a golden sample: two identical pieces signed and dated by both parties, one sealed with each side, with a reference number on the purchase order. A sample cannot show batch consistency, corrosion resistance or life at 200,000 cycles; those need a sampling plan and test reports. This page also lists what to measure on a lock, handle, hinge, closer and glass fitting, and how to write an inspection standard a third-party inspector can apply.
- [Writing Door Hardware Section 08 71 00 in 2026: The Three Parts, What Belongs in Each, and the Clauses That Cost Money](https://cantonlock.com/guides/specification-section-08-71-00-2026/): A door hardware specification is a three-part document with a fixed shape, and most of the money lost on a hardware package is lost by putting the right sentence in the wrong part. This page sets out what belongs in Part 1, Part 2 and Part 3, shows how a hardware set is written so a factory can quote it without a phone call, and names the four clauses that quietly decide the price.
- [Door Handle Spindle Sizes 2026: 8mm and 9mm Squares, Split Spindles, and How to Calculate the Length](https://cantonlock.com/guides/spindle-sizes-and-length-2026/): The spindle is the cheapest part of a door handle set and the one that most often makes a shipment unusable. Three numbers decide whether a handle will turn a lock: the square size, the spindle length, and whether the spindle is solid or split. This page sets out all three, gives the length formula, and shows what our own catalog actually publishes.
- [Stainless Grade Selection 2026: 201 vs 304 vs 316, What Each Costs, and Why "304/201" on a Spec Sheet Is the Real Problem](https://cantonlock.com/guides/stainless-grade-selection-201-304-316-2026/): 201, 304 and 316 look identical in the hand and behave very differently on a building. This page sets out what separates them chemically, where each belongs, what the cost difference actually is, and then does the uncomfortable part, counts how many of our own 313 stainless products name a grade at all, and explains why a specification that says "304/201" has answered nothing.
- [Strike Plates and Keeps 2026: ANSI Strike vs T-Strike, Lip Length, and the Dimension Nobody Measures](https://cantonlock.com/guides/strike-plates-and-keeps-2026/): North America has two standard strike sizes: the ANSI strike, 4-7/8 × 1-1/4in (about 124 × 32mm), for commercial hollow metal frames, and the T-strike, 2-3/4 × 1-1/8in (about 70 × 29mm), for wood jambs, and one cannot replace the other without reworking the frame. This page also covers European keeps, how to work out lip length, square versus radius corners, and why a security upgrade that stops at the lock has upgraded nothing. Models: 575 ABET, 564.
- [Door Hardware Submittal Package 2026: Every Document the Reviewer Needs, and the Four That Get It Rejected](https://cantonlock.com/guides/submittal-package-contents-2026/): A door hardware submittal package has 5 parts: the hardware schedule by opening, a datasheet per catalog number, dimensioned shop drawings, test evidence from an accredited laboratory, and the keying schedule where the project has one. It comes back for 4 omissions: finish names without codes, handing without its convention, a marketing claim where a certificate should be, and no preparation data. From us, drawings, specifications and the catalog are published; a spec export and test documents are sent on request; BIM families and editable CAD are not available.
- [Door Hardware Drawings 2026: PDF, DWG, STEP and BIM Compared, and What a Factory Can Actually Give You](https://cantonlock.com/guides/technical-drawings-what-to-expect-2026/): Asking a hardware factory for "the CAD" produces a different file in every country, and half the time the file you get cannot do the job you wanted it for. This page separates the three kinds of drawing that answer three different questions, compares the formats and what each one is really for, explains why a 3D solid often does not exist even at a competent factory, and states our own drawing coverage as a number rather than a promise.
- [Universal or Handed 2026: Which Hardware Is Reversible, Which Is Not, and the Four Products That Catch Projects Out](https://cantonlock.com/guides/universal-vs-handed-hardware-2026/): "Universal" covers three different things: non-handed (no hand at all, like most butt hinges, plain levers and cylinders), field-reversible (ships in one hand and is turned on site, like most cylindrical, tubular and mortise latches) and factory-handed (one hand only). On a large order, ask for the product supplied reversed to hand and state the split, for example "24 LH, 16 RH". This page also names the four products that are handed when people assume they are not. Models: 575 ABET, 70722 DC.
- [Zinc Alloy Hardware 2026: What Zamak Actually Is, Where It Belongs, and the Four Ways a Bad Casting Fails](https://cantonlock.com/guides/zinc-alloy-die-cast-hardware-2026/): Zinc alloy (zamak, mostly Zamak 3 or Zamak 5, about 4% aluminum) is 28% of the material rows in our catalog, second only to stainless steel at 46%, and buyers distrust it mostly for reasons that describe bad castings rather than the material. This page explains what zamak is, what die casting is genuinely good at, the four distinct ways a poor zinc part fails, where zinc should never be used at all, and what to ask a factory so the answer means something.

### News and insights — short answers to specific questions

- [NBR 11742 and NBR 11785: What a Brazilian Inspection Checks on Fire Door Hardware](https://cantonlock.com/news/brazil-nbr-11742-nbr-11785-fire-door-hardware/): A fire door in Brazil is approved twice, once in the laboratory and once at the AVCB inspection, and the hardware is part of both. What the two ABNT standards ask of a push bar and a pair of doors, what inspectors fail, and what to ask a supplier before the first container. Models: 320, 316-D, 309-D, DC02, 314.
- [One Opening, One Order: The Hardware Set for a Double Fire Exit Door](https://cantonlock.com/news/double-fire-exit-door-hardware-set/): A double fire exit door takes 6 lines of hardware: a device on each leaf, an outside trim on the active leaf, a closer on each leaf, and a coordinator so the inactive leaf closes first. All 6 are sized from 4 facts about the leaves: the width and weight of each leaf, the door thickness, and which leaf is active. This article takes them in that order, shows where 2 correct lines contradict each other, and lists what we need to quote it as one opening. Models: 309-D, 316-D, 320, 023 ET, 023 PS, DC02, DSL02, JU-093 (+1).
- [A Brass Piano Hinge Is Usually Not Brass](https://cantonlock.com/news/brass-piano-hinge-is-a-finish-not-a-metal/): In this trade "brass piano hinge" almost always names the finish, not the metal. Ours is iron under a matt black or polished brass finish, in 1", 1-1/4", 2" and 3" widths, and our own catalog claimed stainless steel until 16 September, which is a good illustration of how the confusion survives. Models: Piano Hinge, BL027, IH01.
- [Entrance, Privacy, Passage: Choosing Between Twelve Cylindrical Locks](https://cantonlock.com/news/choosing-a-cylindrical-lock-entrance-privacy-passage/): 587, 607, 5807, 5870, 592, 598, 575, 578, 9210, 595, 609 and 5831 look like twelve choices and are mostly one choice made twelve times. Nearly all of them take a 60/70mm adjustable backset and a 35–45mm (1-3/8" to 1-3/4") door, so the decision is function first, chassis second, and one of the twelve goes to a 90mm (3-9/16") backset when the others stop at 70. Models: 607 ACBK, 587 MBET, 5807 SSCL, 5870 ACET, 592 SSET.
- [A 25mm Throw and a Collar That Spins: Deadbolts D101 and D102](https://cantonlock.com/news/deadbolt-d101-d102-and-the-rim-alternative/): A deadbolt does one job the latch above it cannot: it throws a solid bolt that no card and no shim will move. Ours throw 25mm (1"), in zinc die-cast with a hardened steel roller pin against sawing, on a five-pin solid brass cylinder, and the free-turning collar is the detail that matters most and photographs least. Models: D101 DSPB, D102 AC, 564, 1073D.
- [45 to 90: Reading Our Euro Cylinder Range](https://cantonlock.com/news/euro-cylinder-range-45-to-90/): In this range the model number is the overall length in millimeters, so 45, 54, 60, 70, 80 and 90 are six lengths rather than six products. All are solid brass. What the letters after the number mean is partly documented and partly not, and this article says which is which. Models: 70 SNDK, 80 SNKT, 45BN, 65SN.
- [650 to 1110mm: Which Push Bar Length Your Door Takes](https://cantonlock.com/news/exit-device-push-bar-length/): Bar length is the dimension most often left off an exit-device inquiry, and the one that cannot be corrected on site. Our published lengths run 650, 800, 900, 1000, 1040, 1050 and 1110mm (43-11/16"), some adjustable and some not, and which of those your door takes is decided by the leaf width rather than by the model you liked. Models: 307, 311, 305.
- [US26D, 626, 630: A Finish Code Is Not a Color](https://cantonlock.com/news/finish-codes-us26d-626-630/): A North American specification writes 626, not "satin chrome". The number encodes the base metal as well as the appearance, so 626 and 652 are the same color and different products. Of 519 published Canton Hyland records, 77 can be given a number honestly; the other 442 cannot, and each has a reason. Models: 5870 ACET, 607 SSET.
- [200,000 Cycles: What the LH Lever Range Is Actually Rated For](https://cantonlock.com/news/lever-handle-range-lh852-lh853-lh855/): LH852, LH853, LH855, 808 and 6491 share a published cycle life of 200,000 operations, a 60/70mm backset, a 35–45mm (1-3/8" to 1-3/4") adjustable door thickness and a solid steel zinc-plated chassis behind a zinc-alloy lever. What separates them is the function set and the shape, and only one of the five offers a dummy. Models: LH853 CPBK, LH855 SNET, 808 ABET.
- [Occupied or Vacant: What a Washroom Indicator Actually Has to Do](https://cantonlock.com/news/occupied-vacant-washroom-indicator-bolt/): An indicator bolt is a lock and a sign in one part: it has to read from standing distance, release from outside in an emergency, and survive several hundred operations a day. Our 200 and 400 are zinc alloy and our 500 is stainless steel, the one for aggressive cleaning or coastal buildings; all are surface mounted, so the door needs no mortise. We do not publish a cycle-test figure or the window size, so ask before you quote against a specification that needs either. Models: 200, 500.
- [The Rim Night Latch: What 564 and 1073 Actually Measure](https://cantonlock.com/news/rim-night-latch-564-and-1073/): A rim night latch sits on the face of the door rather than inside it, which changes every dimension that matters: backset, door thickness range, latch extension and deadbolt throw. The 564 and the 1073 answer the same job in two different metals, and the difference between single-side and double-side is a security decision rather than a convenience one. Models: 564, 564 MB, 1073D, 1073S.
- [Lever Length, Rose Diameter, Projection: The Stainless 9000 Levers](https://cantonlock.com/news/stainless-lever-range-9007-9008-9014/): The 9014, 9007 and 9008 are stainless lever sets on a 53mm (2-1/16") rose for a 35–50mm (1-3/8" to 1-15/16") door. The 9014 publishes a 135mm (5-5/16") lever, 60mm (2-3/8") projection and a 9mm (3/8") rose; the 9007 a 132mm (5-3/16") lever, 63mm (2-1/2") projection and an 8mm (5/16") rose. The 9008 publishes six rows in total, and this article says so rather than filling the gap in. Models: 9014, 9007S, 9008S, 9008E.
- [UL 305 Is a Listing, Not a Grade](https://cantonlock.com/news/ul-305-is-a-listing-not-a-grade/): EN 1125 is a standard you test against. ANSI/BHMA A156.3 is a standard that grades you 1, 2 or 3. UL 305 is neither, it is the basis for a listing, which is an ongoing arrangement with a certification body rather than a document you hold. Confusing the three is how a compliant-looking device fails a submittal. Models: 305, 307, 311.
- [A Padlock Chained to a Knight in Germany](https://cantonlock.com/news/what-an-old-padlock-tells-a-lock-factory/): Our principal found it on a German street, chained around the ankles of a cast-iron knight outside a hotel, and photographed it because the older a thing is the more it draws you in. We cannot tell you who made it or when, rust removes exactly the evidence that would answer that. We can tell you what is still legible in the metal, which is more than you would expect, and why we are not going to invent the rest. Models: 45 SNIK, 60 SNKT, 70 SNDK.
- [Fitting a Euro Cylinder: Five Steps, and the Two Everyone Skips](https://cantonlock.com/news/fitting-a-euro-cylinder/): A euro cylinder goes in and out through the lock case, held by one screw, and the whole job takes two minutes once the cylinder is the right length. Almost every failed fitting is one of two things: the cam was not turned before it was pushed through, or nobody tried the key with the door shut. Models: 70SN, 65SN, 80SN, 45BN.
- [Why a Double Fire Door Needs a Coordinator, and How to Size One](https://cantonlock.com/news/door-coordinator-double-fire-door/): A pair of fire doors with two closers closes in whichever order the springs decide; if the active leaf arrives first, the astragal holds it open and the door does not latch. A coordinator forces the inactive leaf to close first, and it only works when the leaf weights, the closer on each leaf and the coordinator's own rating agree. Our DC02 is rated to 100kg, but our heaviest closer stops at 85kg, so above 85kg we do not currently offer a closer. Models: DC02, JU-093, JU-088, JU-072, JU-073, JU-061, JU-051.
- [Which Exit Device Standard Your Project Is Actually Under](https://cantonlock.com/news/en-1125-or-ansi-which-standard-your-project-needs/): EN 1125 and ANSI/BHMA A156.3 are not two grades of the same thing. They come from different building codes, measure different failures, and a device built to one is not automatically acceptable under the other. The standard is decided by where the door is, not by what you prefer. Models: 307, 305, 310, 311.
- [How Many Levels Your Master Key System Actually Needs](https://cantonlock.com/news/master-key-systems-how-many-levels-you-need/): We build master key systems up to 5 levels, GGMK down to the change key, and most buildings need 3: every extra level spends key combinations the building may need later. This article gives the level chart, a worked example for a 4-floor office with 36 cylinders (the grand master opens all 36, the facilities master 8, the cleaners' sub-master 3) and a blank chart to print and fill in. Models: 70SN, 65SN, 80SN, 45BN.
- [Cross-Referencing a Lock You Already Buy](https://cantonlock.com/news/cross-referencing-a-lock-you-already-buy/): To reorder somebody else's lock, match 6 dimensions, not the model number. For a mortise lock they are backset, center distance, faceplate length and width, case height and depth, spindle size (almost always 8mm square) and door thickness range. Our LC07 85×45mm, for example, has an 85mm center distance and a 45mm backset. Finish names and grade labels do not carry across factories; the dimensions do. Models: LC07 85×45mm, 5681, SSH017.
- [DS013 and DS011 Are Not the Same Kind of Thing](https://cantonlock.com/news/door-stop-holder-or-flush-bolt/): Somebody searched "door stopper ds013 vs ds011" and landed on us. It is a fair question and the answer is that only one of them is a door stopper, DS011 is a flush bolt, which does the opposite job. Here is how to tell three commonly confused items apart before they are on the order. Models: DS013, DS011, DS01, DS05.
- [Cutsheets, CAD and BIM: What We Have and What We Do Not](https://cantonlock.com/news/what-documents-you-can-actually-get/): From us today: specifications on every product page as a table, dimensioned drawings for some models, and one current catalog PDF. Test documents come on request, for the exact model covered. There is no BIM library (no Revit families or IFC objects) and no published door-preparation drawing; for a cutting template, ask for an approved drawing of the exact model. Ask by model number in the configuration you buy: a drawing of the 60mm backset version is not a drawing of the 45mm one. Models: LC07 85×45mm, 70SN.
- [70 Is the Total, Not the Split](https://cantonlock.com/news/euro-cylinder-length-and-split/): The number in 70SN is the overall length of the cylinder in millimeters. It says nothing about how that 70mm (2-3/4") is divided either side of the cam, and the division is the part that decides whether the key turns once the door is hung. Models: 70SN, 65SN, 80SN, 45BN.
- [A Test Report Covers a Model, Not a Range](https://cantonlock.com/news/what-a-test-report-actually-covers/): Our EN 1125 report covers one exit device: KD070/30-290. Our durability report covers one lock: 607 SS ET. Neither covers the family it sits in, and a supplier who lets you believe otherwise has handed you a problem that surfaces at handover. Models: 607 SSET.
- [What OEM Actually Changes, and What It Does Not](https://cantonlock.com/news/what-oem-actually-changes/): Putting your brand on a lock is 4 separate decisions: packaging and marking, branding on the part, finish, and the part itself. Only the fourth needs a mould. This article lists what to send for each of the 4 so the first reply is a real answer. Models: 607 SSET, 70SN.
- [Handing: The One-Letter Answer That Holds Up Orders](https://cantonlock.com/news/handing-left-right-and-universal/): Left, right or universal is a single character on an order line and the most common reason a quotation goes back for clarification. It is decided by where the hinges are and which way the door opens, and the two conventions in use disagree with each other. Models: LC07 85×45mm, LC14 85×50mm, 9001, 587 PBET.
- [The Six Values a Hardware Order Actually Needs](https://cantonlock.com/news/six-values-an-order-needs/): Most inquiries arrive with a model number and a quantity, and most of those go back with a question. Six values decide whether a part can be installed, and an inquiry carrying all six can be quoted the same day. Models: 9001, LC07 85×45mm, 70SN, 587 PBET.
- [Trim Handle or Panic Bar: What the Outside of a Fire Exit Door Needs](https://cantonlock.com/news/trim-handle-or-panic-bar/): A panic bar opens the door from inside. It does nothing for the person outside. The part that lets them in is a separate order line, and getting the two confused is the most common way an exit-door schedule arrives incomplete. Models: 015, 016, 027, 305, 310.
- [ANSI Grade 1 or EN 1125: Which Standard Your Exit Device Has to Meet](https://cantonlock.com/news/ansi-grade-1-vs-en-1125-exit-devices/): They are not two grades of the same thing. ANSI/BHMA A156.3 rates an exit device by cycles and force; EN 1125 tests whether a panicking crowd can get out. Which one you need is decided by the country your building is in, not by which sounds stronger. Models: 001, 023 ET, 027, 309-D, 310, 316-D, 320.
- [Why Aluminum Doors Drop, and What the Lock Case Has to Do With It](https://cantonlock.com/news/narrow-stile-aluminium-door-lock-sag/): A narrow-stile aluminum door that no longer latches has almost never broken its lock: the leaf has dropped a few millimeters at the far edge. On a stile only 30 to 50mm wide, the hinge or pivot side wears first, the frame's corner joints open second, and the latch shows it third, because it sits in a strike with perhaps 2mm of tolerance. Only the lock case is a hardware decision: our narrow-stile cases run at 30, 40 and 45mm backsets. Models: AI8530, LC02 85×40mm, LC03 85×45mm, LC33-5572, LC7065.
- [Push Bar or Touch Bar: Which Panic Device Your Door Needs](https://cantonlock.com/news/push-bar-or-touch-bar-panic-exit-devices/): A push bar pivots and travels; a touch bar depresses flush into its own housing. They cost differently, they fail differently, and only one of them survives a corridor that gets hit by trolleys. Canton Hyland builds the push-bar type across all 42 devices in the range. Models: 001, 015, 023 ET, 027, 310, 316-D.
- [304, 201 or 316: Which Stainless Steel You Are Actually Buying](https://cantonlock.com/news/stainless-steel-grades-304-201-316/): Three grades look identical in a photograph, cost differently, and behave nothing alike within sight of the sea. 201 substitutes manganese for nickel and rusts where 304 does not; 316 adds molybdenum and survives where 304 pits. Here is how to tell which one you have been quoted. Models: LH1033 SS, LH1016, NCB, GL125 SS.
- [What One Frameless Glass Door Actually Needs](https://cantonlock.com/news/what-a-frameless-glass-door-needs/): A frameless glass door is not a product, it is an assembly of six or seven parts ordered from three different categories. Buyers quote the handle, forget the floor spring, and discover the over-panel patch on site. Here is the whole list, in the order it gets forgotten. Models: F101, F110, F112, GL125 SS, 100, 107, D-1031, D-1051 (+7).
- [The Door Schedule: How Hardware Is Actually Specified](https://cantonlock.com/news/door-hardware-schedule-guide/): Projects buy door types, not locks: a schedule says 30 of set HW-01 and 90 of HW-02, and every line in a set has to agree with the others. A lock case with an 85mm center distance needs levers drilled for 85mm and a cylinder sized to the leaf. This article reads a schedule the way a project buyer does, with a worked set (HW-02: an 85mm × 60mm euro lock case, the rows our LC04 publishes), before you quote against one. Models: 001, LC04 85*60, 607 PBBK, F100 SS.
- [Backset and Center Distance: How to Read a Mortise Lock Case Number](https://cantonlock.com/news/mortise-lock-backset-and-centre-distance-guide/): Two numbers decide whether a lock case fits the door, and they are printed in the model number: LC08 85×55 is an 85mm (3-3/8") center distance with a 55mm (2-3/16") backset. 85mm is the standard center distance for euro-profile cylinder locks; backset is where the variation lives, from 16mm cases for narrow aluminum stiles upward. Getting either wrong is the most common reason a container of hardware cannot be installed. Models: LC08 85×55mm, LC04 85*60, LC8520PS, LC34 50×72mm, LC7065.
- [What the Letters After a Model Number Mean](https://cantonlock.com/news/reading-door-hardware-model-numbers/): 607 PB, 607 AB, 607 SN and 607 BN are the same lock in four finishes. The letters are a finish code and a function code, read from the right, and once you can read them a price list of four hundred lines collapses into about sixty products. Models: 607 PBBK, 70710 SN, 70610 SC.

## Guías en español

- [Método de trabado de un dispositivo de salida 2026: de sobreponer, varillas verticales de sobreponer u ocultas, o de embutir, y dónde va cada uno](https://cantonlock.com/es/guides/exit-device-locking-method-2026/): Un dispositivo de salida se elige dos veces: una por las personas que lo van a usar, y otra por cómo traba la puerta. Los de sobreponer traban en un punto en el marco y sirven para puertas de una hoja y puertas dobles con montante central. Las varillas verticales, de sobreponer u ocultas, traban arriba y en el piso y sirven para puertas dobles sin montante, a cambio de un cerradero de piso que hay que mantener limpio. Los de embutir traban mediante una caja de cerradura en el canto. Esta guía explica dónde va cada uno, qué dicen EN 1125 y UL 305 sobre la configuración, y cuál de nuestros dispositivos es cuál.
- [Inspección anual de puertas cortafuego 2026: los herrajes que fallan, del cierrapuertas y el pestillo a las etiquetas, según NFPA 80 y las normas EN](https://cantonlock.com/es/guides/fire-door-annual-inspection-hardware-2026/): Muchas de las observaciones de una inspección anual de puertas cortafuego son de herrajes y no de la puerta: un cierrapuertas que ya no hace entrar el pestillo, un pestillo que no encuentra el cerradero, una puerta acuñada abierta, una etiqueta pintada, un repuesto que nunca estuvo clasificado, una puerta de dos hojas que cierra en el orden equivocado. Esta guía repasa cada observación, según NFPA 80 en Estados Unidos y las normas EN y las reglas nacionales en Europa, y explica qué la corrige normalmente.
- [Importar herrajes para puertas de China a México 2026: Padrón de Importadores, agente aduanal, pedimento, fracción arancelaria y etiquetado NOM](https://cantonlock.com/es/guides/importing-door-hardware-china-mexico-2026/): Importar cerraduras, bisagras y demás herrajes para puertas de China a México sigue un procedimiento público con pasos fijos: RFC activo e inscripción en el Padrón de Importadores del SAT, un agente aduanal autorizado mediante encargo conferido, un pedimento con la fracción arancelaria correcta, el arancel vigente en 2026 para países sin tratado comercial con México, el etiquetado comercial de la NOM-050 cuando aplica, los documentos de origen y un Incoterm acorde con quién importa. Esta guía recorre cada paso sin citar tasas, porque la tasa que cuenta es la vigente para su fracción al momento de importar.
- [¿Bisagras de cobre o de latón? Qué es una bisagra de cobre cuando se piden bisagras de puerta](https://cantonlock.com/es/guides/copper-or-brass-hinges-2026/): Una «bisagra de cobre» que sostiene una puerta es de latón, cobre aleado con zinc; el cobre envejecido es un acabado, no un metal. Dos de nuestras bisagras publican latón como material: la B024, ofrecida de 2,0 a 3,5 mm de espesor, y la B025. Esta página explica qué puede significar la expresión y qué escribir en el pedido para que llegue la bisagra que usted quería.
- [Comparativa de cerraduras cilíndricas y tubulares 2026: cuatro familias, todas las series y qué cambia de verdad el uso pesado](https://cantonlock.com/es/guides/cylindrical-and-tubular-lock-comparison-2026/): 59 cerraduras de perilla y de manija para puerta perforada, en cuatro familias: tubulares, cilíndricas de uso liviano, cilíndricas de uso pesado y comerciales. Lado a lado a partir de sus filas de especificación, con la fila que no las distingue y las que sí.
- [Comparativa de dispositivos de salida 2026: todas las barras antipánico de la gama por largo, trabado y puerta](https://cantonlock.com/es/guides/exit-device-comparison-2026/): 44 registros forman nuestra familia de dispositivos antipánico, y solo 26 son dispositivos de salida. Salvo el pestillo de empuje 315 y la 311 de ABS con aluminio, todos tienen cuerpo de aleación de aluminio y barra de empuje de hierro, así que las tres tablas (puertas de una hoja, de dos hojas y usos especiales) comparan lo que sí cambia: largo, trabado y puerta, con las filas que faltan nombradas.
- [Comparativa de cajas de cerradura de embutir 2026: todas las entradas y distancias entre ejes publicadas, lado a lado](https://cantonlock.com/es/guides/mortise-lock-case-comparison-2026/): 34 de nuestras cajas de cerradura de embutir publican entrada y distancia entre ejes. Aquí están en dos tablas, perfil estrecho y estándar, con las trampas de nomenclatura y las lagunas dichas con claridad.
- [Tabla de entrada y espesor de puerta 2026: qué admiten realmente 589 modelos publicados](https://cantonlock.com/es/guides/backset-door-thickness-chart-2026/): Dos números deciden si una cerradura de repuesto entra en una puerta ya cajeada: la entrada y el rango de espesor. Esto es lo que lleva de verdad nuestro catálogo publicado (contado sobre los registros, no citado de un folleto) con los equivalentes en pulgadas, el método de medida y la cota que no es entrada y se confunde con ella.

Esta página separa los tres tipos de plano que responden a tres preguntas distintas, compara los formatos y para qué sirve cada uno de verdad, explica por qué a menudo no existe un sólido 3D ni en una fábrica competente, e indica nuestra propia cobertura de planos como número y no como promesa.
- [Universal o con mano 2026: qué herraje es reversible, cuál no, y los cuatro productos que pillan a los proyectos](https://cantonlock.com/es/guides/universal-vs-handed-hardware-2026/): «Universal» abarca tres cosas distintas: sin mano (no tiene mano, como la mayoría de las bisagras, las manijas lisas y los cilindros), reversible en obra (sale de una mano y se invierte en el sitio, como la mayoría de los pestillos cilíndricos, tubulares y de embutir) y con mano de fábrica (una sola mano). En un pedido grande, pida el producto suministrado ya invertido a la mano y dé el reparto, por ejemplo «24 LH, 16 RH». Esta página nombra también los cuatro productos que tienen mano cuando la gente supone que no.
- [Herraje de zamak 2026: qué es realmente, dónde va, y las cuatro formas en que falla una fundición mala](https://cantonlock.com/es/guides/zinc-alloy-die-cast-hardware-2026/): El zamak (sobre todo Zamak 3 o Zamak 5, con un 4 % de aluminio aproximadamente) es el 28 % de las filas de material de nuestro catálogo, solo por detrás del acero inoxidable con el 46 %, y los compradores desconfían de él sobre todo por razones que describen fundiciones malas y no el material. Esta página explica qué es el zamak, en qué es genuinamente bueno el moldeo a presión, las cuatro formas distintas en que falla una pieza de zinc mala, dónde no debe usarse nunca, y qué preguntar a una fábrica para que la respuesta signifique algo.

## Every published model

Model number, product name and page, with material and finish in parentheses where
the record carries them. A blank specification on a product page means the figure
is genuinely unpublished, not that the model lacks it.

## Notes for summarisers

- Specification tables are transcribed from the manufacturer's own data. Where a
  field is blank the figure is genuinely unpublished; please do not infer one.
- A certification is listed only against the models named in the corresponding test
  report. Do not generalise a certification across a series.
- Prices are not published. Lead times and MOQ are quoted per inquiry.
